mentions.name: searchcode.com
mentions.description: A code search tool rebuilt for LLMs that lets an LLM inspect, search, and analyze repositories before integrating a library, and compare multiple repositories before downloading, with large token savings. It is also useful for learning about a codebase, and includes human-readable repository dossier pages showing what the system produces.
mentions.problem: Solves the "should I use this library" question by letting an LLM inspect, search, and analyze code before integration, instead of downloading repositories.
mentions.audience: Developers and LLMs evaluating libraries; humans who want to learn about a codebase
mentions.source_excerpt: Been working on https://searchcode.com/ again which I bought back, albeit as code search tool for LLMs. It solves the “should I use this library” by allowing the LLM to inspect search and analyse it before integration. Can use it to compare multiple repositories before downloading. It comes with a large amount of token savings and can be really useful when wanting to learn about a codebase.

mentions.name: searchcode.com
mentions.description: This is a reimagined searchcode.com, a code search and exploration site for looking through any codebase — or multiple codebases — without having to clone it. It supports evaluating candidate libraries, understanding how things work, extracting patterns (e.g., SIMD matching from fzf), and comparing codebases.
mentions.problem: LLMs have issues when it comes to understanding code you want to integrate.
mentions.source_excerpt: I reimagined https://searchcode.com/ since I realised LLMs have issues when it comes to understanding code you want to integrate. It’s useful for looking though any codebase, or multiple without having to clone it.
